what: Trimble makes precise positioning technology: the GPS systems that steer tractors and excavators automatically, surveying instruments, and software that runs construction projects and trucking fleets.
customers: Construction contractors, surveyors, farmers and trucking companies.
money: construction software, machine control and surveying
positioning hardware for agriculture and civil engineering
moat: Positioning hardware and the software that uses it sold together, with correction services and project data that keep customers inside the system once a job is running on it.
risks: A reported net loss of $157M after divestitures and amortisation
Revenue has been flat around $3.7B for four years as hardware was sold off
Construction technology spending follows construction, which follows interest rates
opportunities: $798M of free cash flow despite the accounting loss, about 15 times cash flow
Analysts see about 43% upside, the widest gap among industrial technology companies
The shift from selling hardware once to selling software by subscription raises the quality of the revenue
watch: Annualised recurring revenue growth and the software share of total revenue.
